links.outcome: Correct OPS coding and hallucination counts with versus without retrieved/curated context files
links.effect: Correct coding rose from 44% (no context) to 79% (rules), 70% (examples), 86% (combined); hallucinations fell from 105 to 8, 2, and 6 respectively (p<0.001).
links.quote: Our data strongly support the thesis that contextualization significantly reduces hallucinations and thus leads to a great increase in quality.

links.outcome: Inaccurate GPT-5 OPS code output versus in-hospital ground-truth coding
links.effect: Unenhanced GPT-5 achieved only 44% correct coding, with 132 total mistakes, 105 hallucinations, 9% chaotic LLM failure, and 26% vital mistakes.
links.quote: GPT-5s and GPT-5o showed identical accuracy (44/100 correct codes), followed by GPT-5e (70/100) and GPT-5r (79/100).

links.outcome: Hallucinated or incorrect codes in AI-generated outputs requiring verification
links.effect: Baseline GPT-5 produced 105 hallucinations (misuse and nonsense codes); even the best configuration had 14 mistakes and 6 hallucinations across 100 reports.
links.quote: The main pitfall in practical application is failing to recognize hallucinations as such without verification.

links.outcome: Whether GPT-5 performance generalizes beyond a single-center, single-procedure test to real deployment
links.effect: Authors note single-center, single-procedure testing and say generalizability and local applicability need research before clinical application.
links.quote: However, before clinical application, great research is required focusing on generalizability and local applicability.
